data.description:
## Symptom

A full `make verify` run in a LINKED WORKTREE (macOS, py3.12.13, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`) ends
`19775 passed, 80 skipped, 2 errors` — both errors are teardown failures of the report-only
`_no_repo_root_leaks` autouse guard (`tests/conftest.py:458`), in two innocent bystanders on
two different xdist workers:

```
ERROR tests/unit/test_opcert_rollback_heldout.py::test_revoked_key_backdated_cert_fails_at_storage_anchor
ERROR tests/integration/test_comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py::test_manifest_refuses_incomplete_or_ambiguous_live_jira_population[incomplete]
  Failed: New entries appeared in REPO_ROOT during this test: ['.tickets-tracker']
```

Neither named test creates it: with the entry removed, both plus the 17 modules touched by
`57d2-e356-7eb4-4bf5` pass 182/182 and nothing reappears. They are bystanders — the entry
appeared once inside both of their wall-clock windows, exactly the ambiguity the guard's own
comment documents.

## What actually appeared

```
lrwxr-xr-x  .tickets-tracker -> /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.tickets-tracker   (created mid-run)
```

A SYMLINK to the main checkout's tracker. Only one code path writes that:
`src/rebar/_commands/init.py:198` — when the host repo is itself a linked worktree (`.git` is
a FILE), `init` delegates to `_init_via_symlink`, which does `os.symlink(main_tracker, tracker)`
at `init.py:591`. So some test invokes `rebar init` with the repo root resolving to the
CHECKOUT rather than a `tmp_path` sandbox.

## Why it is invisible in CI

`_init_via_symlink` is reached only when `.git` is a file. CI checks out a normal clone, so the
branch never runs and the leak never appears — this reproduces only for a developer or agent
running the suite from a `git worktree`, which is the workflow `AGENTS.md` and `make worktree`
prescribe. That is the defect: the suite is not sandboxed against the environment its own
contributor guide tells people to use.

## Why it needs fixing rather than tolerating

It is a real isolation leak, not guard noise. The guard is deliberately report-only and removes
nothing, so the symlink is left behind in the worktree; and because the appearance lands in
whatever tests happen to be running, it fails BYSTANDERS, sending the next reader to debug an
unrelated test. Two clean runs in a row can differ only in which tests get blamed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The test that invokes `rebar init` against the checkout is identified by name (bisect the
      suite in a linked worktree with `.tickets-tracker` removed, or trace `os.symlink` /
      `_init_via_symlink`), and the finding is recorded with a `path:line` citation.
- [ ] That test is sandboxed: it initializes under `tmp_path` (or another disposable temp dir),
      never the checkout. Not by widening `_is_framework_artifact`, and not by deleting the
      entry in teardown — the guard's comment explains why attribution-free cleanup is wrong.
- [ ] A full `make verify` in a LINKED WORKTREE completes with 0 errors, and no
      `.tickets-tracker` appears in the worktree root during the run.
- [ ] The regression has an oracle that fails if the leak returns.

## Discovery

Seen while verifying the fix for `57d2-e356-7eb4-4bf5` (theocratic-actuarial-ibex). That change
touches only test fixtures' bare-remote creation and cannot reach `rebar init`; removing the
symlink and re-running every module it touches reproduces nothing. Filed separately so the
leak is tracked rather than absorbed into an unrelated change.
data.title: A test runs `rebar init` against the checkout, symlinking `.tickets-tracker` into a linked worktree and tripping the REPO_ROOT leak guard
